title: VIP Commitment Runway & Prioritization Criteria
creator: Miles Alvarez
description:
Background: As Redwood grows, engineering capacity and roadmap commitments for top accounts must be predictable. Currently we have ad-hoc VIP requests that get routed via support, CSM, and AE teams, leading to uneven commitments, missed expectations, and operational strain.

Objective: Define a repeatable, objective 'commitment runway' for VIP/top-account requests that ties intake signals to a timeboxed commitment policy (runway), explicit prioritization criteria, and stakeholder sign-offs. The goal is to reduce untracked escalations, set clear expectations with sales/CS, and ensure engineering capacity is allocated to work with validated product impact.

Scope: This ticket covers the policy, triage rubric, stakeholder approval flow, and the instrumentation needed in the intake tracker and roadmap board. Implementation work (automation in Zendesk/HubSpot or enforcement in engineering prioritization tooling) will be a follow-up (see dependencies).
acceptance_criteria:
1) A published VIP Commitment Runway policy (Confluence) that defines tiers, quantitative thresholds, and maximum runway windows.
2) Intake rubric that maps signals (ARR, contract terms, strategic partner status, legal/regulatory requirement, platform risk) to a tier and suggested runway length.
3) A signed approval flow template used by CSM, Sales engineer, PM, and Eng lead for any commitment runway > 2 sprints.
4) Instrumentation: sample intake form fields added to the existing intake spreadsheet and a dashboard tile showing outstanding VIP runways and remaining runway days.
5) Stakeholder alignment confirmed via a review doc and cross-functional approval recorded in Confluence.
proposed_solution:
1) Define tiers:
   - Tier A (Strategic VIP): ARR >= $2M, or named strategic partner; runway eligible up to 3 sprints with documented roadmap slot.
   - Tier B (High-value): ARR $500k - $2M or high product dependency; runway up to 2 sprints with conditional approval.
   - Tier C (Emerging): ARR < $500k but time-sensitive or regulatory; runway up to 1 sprint and subject to Product discretion.
2) Triage rubric: combine quantitative signals (ARR, contract SLA clauses, security/regulatory constraints) with qualitative signals (customer pain severity, revenue impact). Each intake auto-scores and maps to a tier.
3) Commitment runway mechanics: timeboxed commitment (number of sprints) documented in intake record; engineering allocates ‘planned runway capacity’ as placeholders rather than guaranteed dedicated headcount.
4) Escalation & fallback: automated fallback rules to default roadmap lane and communication templates if runway cannot be met.
5) Accountability: PM signs off on scope and acceptance criteria; Eng lead signs off on capacity and risk profile; CSM owns customer comms.
6) Automation: add intake fields in our tracker (Google Sheet -> until we wire Zendesk) and a Zap that notifies the PM slack channel when a Tier A intake is created.
rollout_plan:
Phase 1 (2 weeks): Draft policy and triage rubric, gather stakeholder feedback (CS, Sales, Eng leads).
Phase 2 (2 weeks): Pilot with 3 active VIP accounts (agree runway for each), instrument tracker fields and small Zapier notification.
Phase 3 (2 sprints): Iterate on rubric thresholds based on pilot; add Confluence template and communication playbook; update roadmap process docs.
Phase 4 (Q2): Automate intake into Zendesk/Intake tool and add dashboard tile in Console for PM/Eng leads.
Communication: publish to PM guild, CS weekly sync, and exec recap at roadmap review.
metrics:
- % of VIP runways met within committed window (target >= 85%).
- Mean time from VIP intake to PM decision (target <= 5 business days).
- Number of unapproved VIP commitments made (target 0).
- Customer satisfaction for pilot accounts (qualitative + NPS delta).
- Engineering rework hours attributed to runway scope slippage.
stakeholders: Liam Chen - Eng Lead, Serving Runtime
Sofia Martinez - Head of Customer Success
risks:
- Overcommitting engineering capacity and creating technical debt.
- Gameability: Sales/CS may game thresholds to escalate requests.
- Instrumentation gap: until intake is automated, manual tracking may lead to missed entries.
- Legal/contractual SLAs might force higher commitment for certain customers and need legal review.
Mitigations: cap total concurrent runway capacity, require multi-party signoff for Tier A, periodic audit of intake records, and involve Legal for any contract-driven requests.
updates: 2026-02-16: Kickoff meeting with CS & Sales. Agreed to pilot 3 VIP accounts and to use Google Sheet for intake until Zendesk fields are available.
2026-02-20: Draft rubric posted to Confluence for comments (link). CS asked to add 'regulatory hold' as a hard signal; added to rubric document.
2026-02-26: Engineering review: Liam recommends capping concurrent Tier A runway slots at 2 to avoid capacity cliffs. Added hard cap to the proposal.
2026-03-01: Legal input received: any commitment tied to contractual SLA must route through Legal and be excluded from auto-approval. Added to acceptance criteria.

2026-03-05: Pilot enrollments confirmed for Acme Analytics, Finberg Health, and Nova Retail. Created Zapier notification to #pm-vip-intake on Tier A intake. Next: finalize Confluence template and run pilot governance weekly sync.
